In this work, we devise a two-dimensional classical force equation that yields a unique circular motion pattern when time-varying terms are included, resulting in symmetrical off-center circular trajectories with specific parameters.

This paper focuses on examining the limits of fundamental inequalities and solutions to non-local equations on a closed Riemannian manifold. Notably, we demonstrate that there are no optimal solutions to the Sobolev inequality and the Hardy inequality in the context of the Sobolev spaces $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{S}^d)$ and $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{S}^d)$ respectively. This finding offers new insights into the characteristics of the Sobolev and Hardy inequalities on compact manifolds. Moreover, we explore the behavior of solutions to the Laplace equation and its generalization on a compact manifold.

To the best of our knowledge, this study represents a pioneering attempt to develop a probabilistic model capable of inferring the locations of multiple sampling locations based on spatially correlated genetic data. Building upon prior work in single sampling location reconstruction, we introduce a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm to perform concurrent sampling of sampling locations and genetic traits. Employing backward simulation yields superior mixing properties, enabling more accurate convergence in sampling locations compared to traditional Markov chain samplers. Experimental results on simulated and real-world single-nucleotide polymorphism data demonstrate substantial improvements in convergence and posterior accuracy through our proposed approach.

This study examines the small-signal stability assessment of complex grid-connected voltage source converters, taking into account system dynamics modeled in the admittance domain. A new analytical approach provides stability criteria for interconnectors accepting multiple grid-injecting VSCs, grounded or not, by leveraging admittance matrix representations of various grid-injecting configurations. Derived stability criteria are specific to different grid settings: single-injecting, double-injecting, triple-injecting VSCs, and those involving ungrounded converters. A comprehensive stability evaluation matrix offers a systematic framework for assessing the stability of interconnectors injecting multiple VSCs in admittance domain modeling. This study's stability criteria are supported by simulations of small-signal stability analyses.

This paper introduces an approach that enables the creation of high-security online signature verification systems. It outlines a method for extracting and storing unique signature templates in a digital format to prevent forgery. These templates are generated using low-resolution and compressed color images captured on a standard smartphone. The proposed verification method relies solely on pure software implementation, devoid of hardware components. The generated templates are then put to the test through extensive experimentation, demonstrating their ability to accurately validate user signatures across various mediums, including touchscreens, smartphones, and styluses. The performance of this online signature verification system is evaluated through a comprehensive trial involving 40 participants over a prolonged period. The results show an impressive accuracy rate of 99% in recognizing both written and cursive signatures, even after 11 months. The proposed system also exhibits robust security features, including resistance to various forms of tampering and spoofing.

The representations of Hardy sums as area on a triangle are discussed, with a specific method introduced in section \S\ref sec:special and an alternative geometric approach presented in section \V\section{V. Two additional geometric methods exist for expressing Hardy sums as area, one involving a triangle under a line of average value and the other as the area of a trapezoid formed by a flexible membrane, which can be found in appendices \appendix A and \appendix B.

In the 1970s, Joseph Sutherland introduced the concept of inter-process information, encompassing relationships between data structures and algorithms that remain relevant despite changing programs. One such type of inter-process information, referred to as an enduring contextual value, is a stable function linking different program states. This study presents a framework for enduring contextual values, illustrating their connection to abstract memory and illustrating that such values can be categorized hierarchically. By utilizing this framework, it is demonstrated that certain enduring contextual values, specifically those related to information and its updates, are associated with abstract memory. This connection supports a refined understanding of Sutherland's theory and suggests new directions for research in abstract memory.

Human pose estimation from videos has become increasingly significant. A new approach combines the recurrent neural network's (RNN) ability to capture long-term dependencies in time series data with a convolutional neural network's (CNN) spatial dependencies in a single model. A top performing deep neural network for 3D human pose estimation via video is presented. This network employs an encoder-decoder architecture consisting of an initial CNN for feature extraction, followed by an RNN to analyze temporal data, and finally a decoder to predict pose coordinates. To enhance performance, the network utilizes dilated convolutions and attention mechanisms. Experimental results on the SALSAS dataset reveal state-of-the-art results, surpassing all previous methods with a mean squared error of 76.6mm and 82.9mm for 2D and 3D annotations, respectively.

A method known as the Earth occultation method is utilized to assess source intensity by utilizing specific spacecraft as "monocams" that observe the changing Earth transit patterns with limited field-of-view.  Typically, this method is applied to large, uncollimated pixelations in the form of Earth's transmission patterns.  We present an innovative method that leverages the collimated CZTI's capabilities to identify and measure the intensity of transient X-ray sources across the full sky through the use of Earth's transit patterns on the CCDs.  We successfully implemented this technique utilizing CZTI onboard the AstroSat observatory, which has enabled the realization of an all-sky X-ray system known as ASKAS-X-ray (AstroSat Sky Occultation-based All-sky X-ray) using CCDs in the collimated modules.  We have also carried out extensive testing of ASKAS-X's sensitivity and its functionality in identifying all-sky X-ray sources.  We have also demonstrated ASKAS-X's capability to identify and detect X-ray sources through the use of Earth's transit patterns on the CCDs in the presence of the full disk of the Moon.

The efficiency of blockchain protocols can be assessed through their asymptotic behavior. Several studies have made progress in this area, enabling the analysis of network effects on protocol efficiency. This work builds upon the existing results, offering new insights into the efficiency evaluation of blockchain protocols. Specifically, we examine the efficiency of certain consensus models, considering multiple processes and sequences of random events. We provide a more precise characterization of the efficiency of the PBFT protocol and derive stricter conditions required for the consensus model PBFT-C, also introducing a new consensus model called PBFT-D, which is more technologically adaptable.

In our recent chromomagnetic interaction model, we've studied the mass spectra of the doubly heavy tetraquarks, focusing on the $cc\bar{b}\bar{b}$ and $bb\bar{q}\bar{q}$ systems with $q=b,s$. Our analysis revealed the ground state masses of $3.84^{+0.10}_{-0.09}\ \mbox{GeV}$ and $8.98^{+0.12}_{-0.10}\ \mbox{GeV}$ for the $cc\bar{b}\bar{b}$ and $bb\bar{b}\bar{b}$ systems, respectively. Furthermore, we also obtained the decay patterns of the excited states and discussed the properties of the bound states and their internal structures.

We explore the measure hypothesis in the context of electroweak vacuum stability, utilizing an extended measure that depends on a modified effective action, which itself is based on the expectation value of the Higgs field. Although the modified effective action adheres to Standard Model renormalization group equations, it deviates from the standard canonical scalar operator. The relationship between this new measure and the existence of a metastable vacuum is investigated, particularly under the condition where the modified effective action's effective measure becomes infinitely large. The connection between this phenomenon and the appearance of a metastable vacuum is established, along with the possibility that a new, physically observable vacuum may emerge. The implications of this research are also discussed in the context of Grand Unified Theories.

We derive a $q$-Logarithmic Sobolev inequality for functions on a Carnot group with specific non-negative $q$ values within a defined range. Additionally, through further enhancement of the Talagrand inequality, we establish a two-parameter inequality linking the volatility of random variables in a Carnot group and their distributional radius, valid for $1<p<\infty$ and certain $q$ values within a set of possible values.

This work explores the minimum Bregman disparity, a measure that extends various established disparity measures, such as Euclidean, Kullback-Leibler, and $\ell^{\gamma}$ disparities, by employing a smooth function with a single inflection point. The paper addresses two key issues: calculating the Bregman disparity and developing a statistical test for equality in disparity. It demonstrates that the Bregman divergence can be represented as a composite function consisting of the logarithm of the ratio of two functions, enabling the use of Taylor series expansions. This finding facilitates the creation of efficient statistical tests for testing the equality of two distributions based on their sample data. The tests proposed exhibit desirable statistical properties, including the asymptotic validity and asymptotic normality under certain conditions, and their sample versions also exhibit consistency. The effectiveness of the statistical test is illustrated through simulations and a real-world dataset.

We present a novel dynamic Neural Radiance Field approach, wildNeRF, capable of rendering comprehensive dynamic views given only sparse monocular data of the scene. To achieve this, our method employs a dynamic meta-network that adapts to various dynamic objects within a scene, generating a dynamic NeRF model for each object. A comprehensive dynamic scene representation is then obtained by combining the objects within the scene, allowing for the generation of plausibly textured, dynamic objects within a scene, despite only having sparse data of the scene. Notably, our method can capture a range of dynamic phenomena, such as a train moving in a crowded station, a pedestrian walking in front of a train station, and a train approaching while other trains recede in the background. A companion video can be accessed at https://youtu.be/9k3s7o2or5U.

We investigate a discrete version of a statistical measure for infinite random combinatorial quantum graphs, where nodes are connected with uniform edge length. This new metric is analogous to the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy, but it considers the distribution of edge lengths instead of topological graph properties. By utilizing periodic orbit theory, we derive the asymptotic behavior of this metric, specifically that it grows linearly with time.

A novel method has been developed to accurately calculate the periods of periodic variable stars even when their periods are unknown. The approach relies on the inherent symmetry of the data when the data points are shifted by a candidate period. A modified correlation function, referred to as the Periodogram Function, is used to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio of the data by adjusting for these shifts. A simulation study indicates that the Periodogram Function is more effective at identifying the correct period compared to other established techniques, especially when the data is noisy and of limited length. The method has been successfully applied to accurately determine the periods of periodic variable stars in the M31 galaxy using a dataset with 5-day cadence and limited length. The approach has the potential to be utilized in conjunction with other methods, such as the Fourier Transform, to identify periodic variable stars.

A negative imaginary framework can model and design near-ideal controllers for linear, time-varying, or nonlinear systems subject to constraints. A key method for achieving near-ideal controller design involves reformulating a time-varying controller as a negative imaginary framework with time-varying elements. This approach necessitates determining the closest negative imaginary framework with specified time-varying structure under a particular norm. This problem can be formulated as finding the closest negative imaginary matrix in a specific sense. Due to the inherent nonconvexity of this problem, solving it exactly can be challenging. This note demonstrates that the problem can be reformulated as a convex optimization problem under certain conditions on the matrix and its transpose. This reformulation allows for the use of convex optimization techniques to obtain solutions, with an example illustrating their application.

This research presents an innovative, self-updating approach to a language-independent listening system that utilizes continuous improvement without manual intervention. We have successfully integrated advanced listening capabilities, such as enhanced acoustic analysis and text prediction, into a fully automated listening system. As a result, our automated system consistently demonstrates improved performance across all test scenarios, surpassing even its manually trained counterparts. In addition, our approach has been enhanced with automatic speaker profile creation, allowing for personalized performance optimization without the need for manual speech examples. We have also explored the feasibility of real-world applications for our continuous improvement method in various real-world scenarios, such as enhanced speaker recognition systems.

This research paper presents our contribution to SemEval-2020 Task 9 on Emotion in Social Interactions (ESI). We introduce an innovative method for classifying emotions in real-time multilingual conversations by translating all utterances into a common language and training a deep neural network to identify emotional cues. We assess the effectiveness of this approach using a specially designed dataset featuring Spanish-English and Chinese-English conversations. Experimental results show that our proposed framework can successfully detect emotions in multilingual conversations with moderate precision.

We investigate a fully consistent model incorporating the Type-III seesaw mechanism and small-scale leptogenesis for generating the correct neutrino mass and leptogenesis baryon asymmetry.  By combining the Type-III seesaw with a second Higgs doublet and a right-handed Majorana neutrino, our three-loop radiative seesaw model, which includes a right-handed neutrino with a mass below 10 MeV, successfully explains the observed value of the neutrino mass and leptogenesis baryon asymmetry.  By incorporating the model's Yukawa couplings to the right-handed neutrino, we obtain the required neutrino mixing elements and, using the seesaw formula, relate them to the mass of the right-handed neutrino.  By applying the small-scale leptogenesis mechanism, we demonstrate that the model can produce the correct baryon asymmetry, which is consistent with observations, particularly in the presence of a small right-handed neutrino mass.  By extending the model to include dark matter candidates, our results show that the model's right-handed neutrino can be considered as a dark matter candidate, which is supported by the fact that the model's right-handed neutrino is not affected by the right-handed neutrino mass.

User reaction forecasting, a crucial task in social media platforms involving predicting the likelihood of users reacting to future posts, presents an intriguing challenge due to the vast array of possible reactions. This challenge is compounded by the limited data for new users and users who engage in specific activities. Existing research on user reaction forecasting is largely based on traditional methods that rely on collaborative filtering and graph structure, which are hindered by scalability issues and struggle to adapt to evolving content types. This paper proposes an innovative approach to user reaction forecasting that utilizes item-based neural networks and incorporates item-specific and user-specific attention mechanisms to generate personalized reactions. By employing this approach, our proposed model demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models on public datasets, and it also exhibits adaptability in handling new users and various item types without requiring additional training.

In an effort to improve the performance of cell-free networks, intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) are incorporated into the system, however, their effectiveness is significantly impacted by uncertainty in their reconfigurable elements. This paper proposes an advanced framework that combines collaborative filtering and deep learning to address this challenge. The framework's first step involves developing a model to predict the behavior of IRS under uncertain conditions, and its second step involves determining the optimal transmit beamforming and power adjustments. The results of the analysis show that the framework's performance is near-optimal and improves with the presence of multiple IRSs. The framework also demonstrates its ability to adapt to changing environments and effectively handles complex scenarios with multiple resources.

Dynamic branch forecasting, a crucial component of compiler optimization, has garnered significant attention from the research community in recent years. This study conducts an in-depth examination of deep learning-based approaches to dynamic branch forecasting, a challenging task that involves predicting branch outcomes using input values. Our investigation compares the predictive capabilities of various deep learning methods, including different types of neural networks, against a leading approach based on support vector machines (SVM). Our findings suggest that support vector machines consistently outperform neural networks in this context. Furthermore, we delve into the effects of neural network design on performance and propose novel approaches to improve forecasting accuracy. Our proposed models exhibit competitive outcomes in predicting branch outcomes for x86-64 binaries, achieving 93.5% average accuracy and reducing errors by 23.5% relative to the existing state-of-the-art technique.

A key aspect of the internet of things is the ability to perform active sensing through active camera management, where the location of one or more cameras is actively controlled to produce desired outputs. In this study, we investigate active camera management using a unique combination of deep neural networks and a mimicry-based approach. Our proposed method uses a deep convolutional neural network to mimic the behavior of a human expert that demonstrates optimal camera control techniques. The experimental results of our method using the MNIST and Street View Feet datasets show significant improvement in the accuracy of active camera management compared to a conventional passive camera management policy. Furthermore, our method's accuracy exceeds that of a traditional human expert in the absence of optimal conditions, meeting or exceeding the expert's performance.

For a lattice model of interacting spins, where the interaction energy is directly proportional to the product of nearby spins and decreases proportionally to their spatial separation, we've developed a non-linear system of equations that represents the limiting behavior of Gibbs measures. The system's fixed points are shown to be the limiting Gibbs measures as the interaction energy approaches a critical point. The derivation of this system utilizes an extension of a nonlinear martingale approach, adapted to the SOS framework, and incorporates a disparity mechanism to address the challenges posed by unbounded spin variables and lattice dimensions. The mechanism is successfully applied to a non-homogeneous model of interacting spins, where the local interaction energy is a function of the spin values and their spatial separation, and where the resulting model is a non-linear system of disparity equations. The model's fixed points are shown to be the limiting Gibbs measures as the interaction energy approaches its critical point.

A theoretical framework for modeling the coupled dynamics of light and matter is presented, drawing on the principles of quantum mechanics to describe the probability of energy exchange between photons and the material's energy levels. This framework enables the computation of photon and excitation state population dynamics in a medium consisting of two levels, where the energy levels are not necessarily the same, allowing for a wide range of media, including those containing molecular groups with multiple resonances. The framework's accuracy is validated through comparison with established models in specific cases.

The form factors of charmed and bottom mesons coupled with light vector mesons are calculated using QCD sum rules, with a detailed analysis of their behavior both at short and long distances. This involves determining the strong coupling constants, including radiative decays of vector mesons into meson pairs, with a focus on their role in extracting physical parameters like mixing angles, masses, and decays of quarkonia. This study specifically calculates the coupling strength of certain radiative decays and provides a comprehensive understanding of the nature of interactions involved. Additionally, it explores the potential of certain radiative decays as sensitive probes for CP violation in systems like B, Y, and their respective decays into vector mesons.

Future neutrino experiments will thoroughly test various aspects of neutrino physics and play a crucial role in resolving some outstanding questions. This document provides a concise, non-technical overview of key neutrino experiments that are set to resolve important uncertainties in the field within the next few decades. It covers long-baseline beam experiments, neutrino oscillations in matter, CP violation, sterile neutrinos, and other open questions. It also touches on cutting-edge technologies like radio-frequency cavities, advanced plastic detectors, and laser-computed tomography, which will significantly contribute to these experiments' capabilities. Although this document cannot delve into the extensive technical details of these experiments, it aims to provide a clear and accessible explanation of the significance and potential of these neutrino trials.

The primary goal of this research is to establish a theoretical framework for exploring these mechanisms using regression analysis. It delves into the implications of various procedures for quantifying the causal effects of a particular factor on a variable, taking into account the existing relationships between variables. Through theoretical examination, it identifies both limitations and guaranteed outcomes based on the design of these regression models. This investigation focuses on the conditional linear model, considering a scenario where a variable is influenced by multiple factors with differing directions of effect. It also touches on the more complex scenario involving mixtures of both positive and negative causal influences. The discussion includes several topics: understanding the limits of shrinkage estimation, identifying the problem of bias caused by confounding variables, and the use of instrumental variables. It also provides a solution for estimating the average causal effect across a range from zero to one, and outlines a method for estimating the range of the average causal effect. This research concludes by applying its framework to the use of regression adjustment in the estimation of causal effects. It highlights the potential for this method to produce unbiased results when properly applied. This research is a condensed version of the author's PhD thesis.

This paper presents a novel control method that leverages wide-area measurement systems to enhance power system damping through voltage source converters. By utilizing natural damping signals, this approach prevents data transmission delays and signal loss, and demonstrates that WAMS-driven damping controllers can improve damping performance and reduce energy consumption. A practical implementation of this method is shown using time-delayed state feedback control, and its effectiveness is validated using an academic power system model with multiple damping signals.

We investigate the effects of two-atom degradation on subradiance in large groups of identical two-level atoms under specific excitation conditions that prevent individual atom excitations. This study reveals that, in an N-atom collection without this degradation, steady-state subradiance occurs only in even-numbered atoms within the collection. However, when two-atom degradation is present, subradiance can arise in odd-numbered atom collections, including collections of the total collection N. The degree of subradiance increases as two-atom degradation becomes more significant. Additionally, we examined the second-order correlation function for two-level atoms experiencing two-atom degradation and found that, in the absence of this degradation, subradiance is characterized by a zero-frequency suppression in the correlation function. Conversely, in the presence of two-atom degradation, subradiance is associated with positive correlation function values at zero frequency.

We are investigating a mathematical model describing a nonlinear elastic rod with internal oscillations. When subject to an odd, complex disturbance, we show that the stability of the kink solution is demonstrated by the convergence of the solutions to a modified wave equation to those of a wave equation. The key proof lies in an advanced energy-based multiplier method combined with Loomis-Whitney min-max convolution techniques.

This note assesses the feasibility of creating a high-intensity proton beam utilizing the J-PARC hadron beam line, 20-1, to experimentally verify color transparency through the production of high-energy, forward particles from heavy nuclear targets. Given the constraints of current technical capabilities at J-PARC, experiments proposed in the past, including those of the past and the current long-term plan, are found to be under technical limitations. Consequently, this report outlines potential adjustments to experimental proposals to optimize the production of suitable high-energy, forward particles and facilitate accurate observations supporting or refuting color transparency.

The success of human expertise in games like Go, Billiards, and Tennis motivates researchers to develop artificial intelligence with comparable abilities. To achieve this, most recent studies focus on developing a policy by interacting with a single, continuous environment. However, our research reveals a new approach that considers a discrete environment as a grid-based grid, which can be trained using a policy network that mimics human opponents through consistent training. Furthermore, our proposed method can be enhanced by integrating virtual opponent discrete perturbation, a strategy that randomly changes the opponent's grid-level strategy to make it more challenging. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, which outperforms the original version in games like Go, Billiards, and 8-Board Checkers.

This paper introduces a cutting-edge medical image deep learning model called MFCETT, designed specifically for detecting polyps using a single endoscope. MFCETT stands for Multi-frame Feature Concatenation and Endoscopic Temporal Transformation network, and it introduces a unique frame cooperation mechanism to improve the accuracy of polyp detection. By combining features from multiple frames, frame shifts, and a custom transformation layer, MFCETT enables the model to learn and adapt to different polyp shapes and movements. The proposed MFCETT model is then trained using a large endoscopic polyp dataset, and its performance is evaluated using a custom-built endoscopic polyp detection pipeline. The results show that MFCETT outperforms other advanced models, and it can even match the accuracy of human annotators. Moreover, MFCETT achieves a high accuracy of 94.7% in identifying polyps and 5.3% in identifying false positives. The source code of MFCETT is publicly available on GitHub.

This paper proposes a novel method that allows a sequential sampling process to uncover the characteristics of a dynamic stream consisting of diverse items, each arriving at unpredictable times. Our approach is designed to accommodate a wide range of arrival rates, making it more resilient to sudden spikes in the volume of items in the stream. Our goal is to uncover the relative frequencies of various categories within the stream using an adaptive sampling technique that minimizes unnecessary queries over time. Our approach ensures not only that a precise count of each category is obtained but also that a confidence level associated with this count is also determined. Our method has been proven to achieve this goal accurately, and we have also verified its efficiency through experimental results.

A significant $rp$-process anomaly was discovered when a $^{57}$Zn isobar was produced, as its decay did not include delayed $\beta$-decay but instead resulted in $\beta$-delayed proton emission.  This finding confirms that $^{57}$Kr decays into $^{57}$Zn via the weak interaction, and further demonstrates that the $rp$-process bypasses the $^{56}$Ni stability point.  The data collected from this phenomenon can be used to enhance existing $rp$-process models.

We consider a linear sequence of curves in a complex torus and establish that the closure of rational solutions within this sequence has rational properties, specifically, it is comprised of translates of lower-dimensional abelian subgroups - either abelian subgroups of the sequence or their higher-dimensional products.

A selection of known pulsars in the Northern Sky was investigated for gamma-ray emission detected over a wide energy spectrum, spanning from 160 GeV to 10 TM TeV, utilizing the VERITAS telescope, a gamma-ray observatory featuring a ground-based array of four imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes. Data collected through observations conducted between 2008 and 2015 were analyzed, including the first results from a multi-object study focusing on six pulsars. None of the observed pulsars displayed significant radiation levels exceeding 5 standard deviations, with only the pulsar PSR J0943+205 and a nearby source, MGRO 5J2010+54, showed slightly elevated emission levels at the level of about 2 standard deviations, with MGRO 5J2010+54, in turn, showed slightly elevated emission levels at the level of about 2 standard deviations, with further analysis required to determine its nature.

This paper examines the extended behavior of reaction-diffusion equations with non-local boundary conditions.  The existence and uniqueness of solutions for the original initial boundary value problem are proven, along with a comparison principle, under a specific condition.  It is shown that the solution exhibits long-time boundedness and approaches a steady-state through a series of asymptotic analyses.  Notably, the original equation can be approximated by a modified reaction-diffusion equation with a larger Laplacian, leading to two key findings: the solution's time derivative is bounded globally, and the solution's decay rate at infinity can be estimated.  Theoretical results are illustrated through numerical examples in one and two dimensions.

We have developed a novel approach, UCG-XAI, which utilizes the XAI framework to analyze the internal structure of clusters and identify ultra-compact dwarfs and globular clusters. This approach is based on UCG-XAI, a machine learning tool that classifies UCM/X-ray-bright DDFs and GGCs. Our test with the UCM-XAI classifier achieved a success rate of 0.93, while the GGC-XAI classifier achieved a rate of 0.87. Utilizing the X-ray luminosity function of the UCM-XAI classifier, we discovered 57 potential UCM/X-ray-bright DDFs and GGCs candidates within the MCG dataset. Our UCG-XAI analysis of the LFRS dataset revealed 12 potential UCM/X-ray-bright DDFs and GGCs candidates. Our GGC-XAI analysis of the LFRS dataset revealed 8 potential UCG candidates. Our UCM-XAI analysis of the MCG dataset revealed 55 potential UCM/X-ray-bright DDFs and GGCs candidates, with 8 being previously identified in the SERS findings.

Recommendation systems are a vital component in numerous e-commerce and media platforms, generating enormous revenue for companies like Netflix and Amazon. A key aspect in developing these systems involves running substantial simulations with millions of users to fine-tune the algorithms and pinpoint the most effective strategies. In this research, we delve into the intricacies of these massive user simulations, focusing on overcoming the obstacles posed by scalability and data protection issues. Specifically, we explore the creation of a lightweight synthetic user dataset suitable for simulation purposes, without compromising on recommendation accuracy. Our objective is to uncover opportunities for algorithmic enhancements, allowing companies to implement targeted updates and streamline the development process. Moreover, we investigate the efficacy of simulating the user experience through fast online Monte Carlo methods, shedding light on the discrepancies between real-world data and simulated environments that can impact recommendation metrics.

We investigate the convergence of a truncated sample average when the distribution of the random variable $X$ is extremely large, with conditions that depend on the quantile of $X$. A new method is proposed, which examines the truncated sample average at a specific point, the minimum value of the distribution, in order to establish convergence bounds. By using this method, we can determine the optimal truncation point that balances the variance and variance of interest in statistical inference, particularly in hypothesis testing. As a result, we can establish a general convergence bound of the sample average and propose a new estimator that achieves optimal asymptotic variance under heavy-tailed distributions.

A proposed convolutional neural network architecture incorporates the advantages of Gaussian filters and removes the requirement for pre-processing of raw EEG signals. By using a neural network with sine filters and eliminating the need for pre-processing the raw EEG signals, this design allows for improved motor-imagery classification and offers enhanced generalization. By utilizing a neural network with sine filters and eliminating the need for pre-processing of raw EEG signals, this design allows for improved motor-imagery classification and offers enhanced generalization. The presented convolutional neural network outperforms traditional deep learning methods when applied to motor-imagery BCI tasks.

In this second paper on noncommutative $AdS_2$, our findings show that the AdS/RR field equations in $d=2$ dimensional space-time can be derived from a noncommutative version of the $O(d,2)$ conformal group. We establish that the structure of conformal symmetry in $O(d,2)$-gauged $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity is preserved in the commutative limit, with the resulting AdS/RN black hole solution obtained through this method exhibiting unique features such as an absence of electric or magnetic hair. Notably, the solution's entropy exhibits an interesting double logarithmic scaling as the string coupling tends to zero. We also explore the solution's properties under $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetry. An alternative derivation of the solution is presented through the use of the relation principle. We find that the AdS/RN background is part of a broader set of noncommutative $AdS_2$ solutions that can be naturally obtained from a noncommutative version of the $O(d,2)$ conformal group.

The problem of selecting an optimal pair of kidneys for transplant, out of a given set, is a generalization of the bi-kar matching problem, where solutions must adhere to the rule of one kidney per recipient and one recipient per kidney. This is analogous to the classic hospital-residents matching problem, where we consider each kidney as a job and recipients as hospitals. In the context of kidney transplants, this pairing is temporally sequential and incompatible in the short term, leading to the definition of short-term incompatibility in this work. Based on temporary incompatibility, we have formulated the short-term incompatibility kidney exchange system (SICKES) and the short-term incompatibility kidney pairing problem (SICKPP). To address SICKPP, we have developed the concept of ideal acceptance, which aims to maximize the total surplus of satisfied pairs. This includes short-term and long-term incompatibility constraints, where the latter arises from the selected pair's incompatibility. To tackle SICKPP, we have devised a novel integer programming formulation and a polynomial-time algorithm, building on the concept of path decomposition. Furthermore, we have established a 2-approximation algorithm for SICKPP.

Sequence classification is a fundamental machine learning objective with various applications, including speech recognition, text analysis, and medical diagnosis. This work compares the performance of three models - Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Hidden Markov Model (HMM), and a hybrid model combining LSTM and HMM. The study evaluates the effectiveness of these models for sequence classification tasks using two datasets from the Kaggle platform: Amazon review sentiment analysis and New York City crime type prediction. Experimental results indicate that a hybrid approach utilizing LSTM and HMM outperforms the individual models in sequence classification.

We examine some fundamental characteristics, such as compactness, Fattah-Samchuk Wiener-Hopf, and invertibility of a specific type of algebraic object, namely the generalized Volterra integral operator, $V_\beta$, within weighted Bergman spaces in the open unit disk, $\mathbb{D$. Additionally, we investigate the connection between $V_\beta$ and a related operator, $T_f$, derived from a function, $f$, and determine conditions under which $T_f$ shares key properties with $V_\beta$.

Large-scale online surveys are a vital means of communication in various settings, including customer feedback and language development research.  At a global scale, platforms such as Qualtric play a crucial part in conducting these online surveys.  The company Qualtric handles massive volumes of data from over 90 countries, totaling more than 100 million responses annually.  To improve the efficiency of cross-language image-choice and multi-selective question types, Qualtric employs the MIMIC model, which offers superior performance.  However, these models consume significant storage space, which hinders data distribution and deployment.  To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach to compressing MIMIC models using vector quantization.  This technique achieves high data compression ratios while preserving model efficacy.  At Qualtric, we successfully implemented this method to reduce storage space for the MIMC model from 2.5TB to 750GB.  Moreover, we found that these compressed models exhibit minimal performance decline, and in some instances, they even offer comparable accuracy to the original models.  This solution has been production-ready since 2021 and remains in use at Qualtric.

One of the most pressing issues in modern data science is finding a balance between releasing valuable information and maintaining confidentiality. This paper explores the concept of 'data revelation' by defining it as the process of making individual data points publicly accessible, subject to certain conditions. Two key elements form the foundation of this idea: firstly, a data revelation is only legitimate when it benefits both parties (the data provider and the consumer); secondly, a data revelation is only successful when it leverages the unique properties of the data as a whole. By examining the current state of data science, we can identify the limitations of existing methods in handling sensitive data, which often rely on restrictive assumptions or inadequate protection. In response, we introduce a data representation model based on a combination of a data graph and a potential function, enabling us to pinpoint and modify sensitive data with minimal disruption. This approach is then applied to three applications: private data publishing, federated learning, and differential privacy. Through these examples, we demonstrate how data revelation can be effectively utilized to strike a balance between privacy and utility. Ultimately, we conclude by highlighting the potential for data revelation to revolutionize data science and outline areas for further research.

This paper presents two types of decomposed Richelot mappings, which involve translating symplectic isomorphisms between Jacobian varieties of hyperelliptic curves into isomorphisms between associated Richelot isogenies of these curves. The first type of mapping corresponds to translations in the Fuchsian group by an element that doubles its period, while the second type corresponds to translations by an element that does not double the period. Applying these mappings to the case of generalized Howe curves yields a single decomposed Richelot mapping, which can be used to relate the Jacobian variety of a generalized Howe curve to isomorphisms between Richelot isogenies of specific coverings of the curve.

Recent studies of magnetic hot subdwarf stars have led to a theory that they may have originated from mergers of close binary systems, which could explain their unusual magnetic properties. However, most known magnetic hot subdwarfs are single-lined spectroscopic binaries, which may indicate that binary status is not a requirement for magnetic fields. To explore this idea, researchers have conducted an analysis of three single-lined spectroscopic hot subdwarfs discovered through the LAMOST open galaxy catalog. The analysis revealed that two of the stars show broad, resolved spectra that are consistent with binary systems, while the third star shows a broad, fixed-line profile. The spectra of the binary stars changed over time, which suggests that they are likely merger products. Furthermore, a detailed analysis of the stars has revealed properties consistent with merger remnants, including low masses and expanded sizes. The analysis also revealed that the merger remnants have magnetic fields stronger than those found in binary stars of similar properties. The findings suggest that merger remnants may have stronger magnetic fields than those found in binary stars of similar properties.

We examine the task of identifying the matrix rank from a singular positive semi-definite matrix X, consisting of 'n^2' entries. Although this problem can be solved efficiently using eigenvalue decomposition of X, this requires O(n^3) operations. Our approach simplifies this process by directly estimating the matrix rank r, achieving this by applying a new method of Gaussian reduction with volume selection. Matrix multiplication and the associated 'add-subtract' operations are utilized to achieve this. Our method is based on a new approach of Gaussian reduction with volume selection. Our method is able to determine the matrix rank in O(r^3 + r^2n) operations and is O(r^2n^2) in complexity. Our approach also has an associated statistical error bound. Our approach is also known as the 'Rational' method. Our method is more efficient in terms of its computational power and statistical error when compared to existing methods, especially when the matrix rank is lower than or equal to the square root of the total number of entries in the matrix.
