Our investigation is motivated by a previous study, in which this second dataset was found to be susceptible to artificially induced noise, as well as a new method known as Spectral Contrastive Loss which was proposed to counter this limitation. However, in our work, we discover that the approach is not entirely effective and that the problematic signals still persist. Consequently, we propose that the problematic signals can be identified using a combination of their spectral and temporal characteristics, serving as a supplementary tool to the Spectral Contrastive Loss method.

A theoretical analysis of two-component fermions with SU(N) symmetry has been conducted, and it's shown that, under certain conditions, an exotic phase with broken symmetry, referred to as nomadic ferromagnetism, can occur in this system. Characterized by a fluctuating, non-topological order parameter, this phase is marked by a specific type of long-range order that persists even when a confining potential is applied. Furthermore, it's found that this order is highly stable and can be maintained across a broad range of parameters, and an experimental study of two-component fermions with U(N) symmetry has provided evidence for the existence of this phase in fermions with multiple components.

The primary goal of our study is to uncover the underlying distribution of L-brightness and D-distance of gamma-ray pulsars. To achieve this, we have employed a novel approach known as "soft evidence" in our analysis. We have successfully utilized this method to obtain a 3D probability density map of pulsars, which we have been able to validate through a thorough comparison with independent analyses and by replicating previously established relationships between pulsar luminosity and orbital parameters. Our investigation has led to a series of significant discoveries, including the discovery of two distinct subpopulations of gamma-ray pulsars - low-luminosity stars clustered near the Galactic center and more luminous stars situated at the Galactic disk.

In the realm of strongly correlated quantum systems, a specific phenomenon known as magnetoroton is distinguished by an extensive degeneracy and a vast spectral range. Building upon recent advancements in understanding magnetorotons within the fractional quantum Hall system, we investigate the properties of a two-dimensional XY model in the presence of a magnetic field, revealing an extensive degeneracy and a vast spectral range for magnetorotons. The presence of these magnetorotons is observable through their connection to the ground state's topological entropy. Utilizing the theory of conformal field, we demonstrate that the total regulation of the long-distance wave function is influenced by the energy scale, a phenomenon previously observed only in one-dimensional systems. Furthermore, we establish that the XY model is capable of regulating the long-distance wave function in the presence of a magnetic field, a phenomenon that is also capable of being detected. Our analysis also reveals that the XY model exhibits a specific type of regulation that is independent of the magnetic field, a phenomenon that is unique to two-dimensional systems. The results obtained in this study are expected to have a significant impact on the understanding of quantum many-body systems and may provide new avenues for the discovery of new states of matter.

The NEF experiment aims to measure energy events in a target made of graphite within a vacuum chamber through the use of sensors located at the end of long bores. The interplay of high-energy particles and gas molecules in the target material results in the formation of radiation patterns that can be analyzed through the spatial and spectral distribution of the X-rays produced. The experiment's key components are discussed in detail, including the sensors employed for the measurement of energy events, the precision timing and positioning of the X-ray detectors, and the sophisticated data acquisition system. The results of the performance tests of the instruments are also presented.

A rigorous proof of the Cauchy existence and uniqueness theorem is lacking for the truncated Boltzmann equation. However, when initial conditions are sufficiently small, the influence of past collisions diminishes, allowing the possibility of controlling past data. This idea underlies the research outlined in this work, specifically for $N$-truncated Boltzmann equation systems in multi-dimensional space with mild regularization, applying a modified Hartree-Fock factorization and a time-weighted $L^2$ norm decay estimate for controlling past data.

Classifiers developed using noisy labels within a training dataset may
systematically misclassify certain instances, hindering their overall reliability. 
Noise during the learning process can significantly impair a classifier's
ability to learn.  This study investigates the resilience of classifiers against
noise.  Our research focuses on developing a robust image classifier against
noise, evaluated on the CIFAR-10 dataset with a noisy label rate of 20% and
intentionally added misclassifications.  Our findings indicate that a
multi-label classifier trained with a combination of logistic regression,
Bayes' theorem, and a soft-tie technique exhibits resilience to label noise. 
The soft-tie approach significantly outperformed standard hard-classification
techniques, yielding an improved accuracy of 6.5% on the test set. 
Additionally, the soft-tie approach efficiently identified noisy training data
points, achieving an accuracy rate of 97%.

A self-adjoint operator can be defined on the set of all automorphism ensembles of a finite field extension $\mathbb{F}_q^m$. This operator's eigenvalues fall within the set of rational numbers, and it has a maximum eigenvalue of $q^m$. Notably, the size of any automorphism ensemble is given by the absolute value of the corresponding eigenvalue. Furthermore, the properties of the eigenvalues have been fully characterized for the specific case of separable orbit codes. Moreover, it has been proven that the size of any automorphism ensemble $\phi$ in relation to the size of the corresponding orbit code $\mathcal{C}(\phi)$ is bounded by the inequality: $|C(\phi)| \leq (q^m - \kappa(\phi))^{1/m} \cdot |\mathcal{C}(\phi)|$.

A precise mass measurement of a star at the cluster's turnoff has been achieved for M67, an ancient open cluster with a verified age of 4 billion years. The precise mass measurement was made possible by combining the cluster's kinematic data with the stellar rotation rates of a Sun-like star, which is the cluster's second most massive star. The rotation rates were used to correct for the stellar evolution models and estimate the cluster's mass. The resulting mass for M67 was $1.82 \pm 0.10 M_\odot$, which is consistent with the predicted mass derived from Y$^2$ model simulations. The precise mass measurement has further confirmed the accuracy of the Y$^2$ model simulations, which had previously been validated for younger and more massive clusters. The precise mass measurement has also verified the cluster's kinematic data, which are consistent with the predicted values from the Y$^2$ model simulations.

We introduce a new concept involving the $\alpha$-stark effect for the complex Schrödinger operator $\mathscr{L}_c = -d^2/dx^2+cx^\alpha$, extending existing work on sufficiency. This work will serve as a basis for further investigations, such as analyzing the $\alpha$-stark effect's essential spectrum. The $\alpha$-stark effect is a crucial area where new insights can be applied to the $\alpha$-stark modified harmonic oscillator.

A revised, more efficient and accurate method of SPH has been developed by refining several key areas. The revised method involves a more precise approach to evaluating the consistency of weights across the mesh and a more targeted method of calculating density gradients. Additionally, the spatial and time-based precision of the revised SPH code has been increased, enabling it to perform complex tasks such as calculating the positions and velocities of particles with greater accuracy. The results show that the revised method reduces the discrepancy between the average density and the density at the center of the mesh, and it also increases the stability of the pressure and density terms. The revised code has been successfully applied to simulate a complex scenario involving a drop impacting a smooth, solid surface and it has demonstrated improved accuracy compared to previous versions.

Capturing high-quality color images often requires significant exposure, resulting in images comprised of multiple photosensitive pixels and pure spectral pixels. These two types of pixels contain valuable information about scene reflectance, which can be combined to reconstruct high-fidelity spectra for accurate color image reproduction. However, current spectral super-resolution methods fall short due to differences between pure spectral and multi-pixel images. To address this limitation, we introduce a new end-to-end deep spectral super-resolution network that learns to combine the information from multi-pixel and pure spectral pixels. By developing a novel loss function that incorporates spectral and pixel-sensitive penalties, and using a spatial transformer module for effective spectral resampling, our network significantly improves spectral reconstruction quality and color image accuracy. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world data confirm the effectiveness of this approach, demonstrating superior performance to existing state-of-the-art methods.

In computer vision, a significant issue is pinpointing the location of objects within large images. To address this, a new approach to geotagging is introduced in this paper, a computer vision task focused on assigning spatial coordinates to objects. The proposed geotagging method involves training a deep learning model to predict geotags for objects in large, low-resolution images. The model is developed using a unique, self-supervised learning method that leverages the availability of high-resolution data. The proposed method features a novel loss function and a training procedure that enables the model to transfer knowledge effectively from high-resolution to low-resolution data. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach, yielding impressive accuracy on a large dataset.

The process of dam storage retrieval is critical for dam safety and risk assessment. The study presents a machine learning framework that utilizes remote sensing data to estimate dam storage. The framework consists of two stages: first, it generates digital topographic maps from satellite imagery, and then it applies custom metric learning to predict dam storage from satellite or satellite-like imagery. The proposed method outperforms conventional machine learning baselines in dam storage retrieval, requiring only limited training data. The framework's flexibility allows it to be applied not only to dam storage retrieval but also to any remote sensing problem requiring only topographic context.

This paper introduces a new quantitative measure called QFS-area, which assesses the extent of Feasible Regions in nonlinear optimization problems. By examining a wide range of known examples, it reveals a surprising correlation that previous results had failed to identify earlier.

This study aims to demonstrate the effectiveness of text-image multi-modal learning in predicting store categories during a shopper's initial attraction, such as a retail store's entrance or location. The goal is to better understand customer preferences by analyzing shopping centers' marketing materials, like websites and social media, to identify relevant products and enhance targeted advertising efforts. We have assembled a dataset containing a subset of a large e-commerce platform's information on shopping centers and products. This dataset contains a substantial amount of text and image data, along with category labels. We have developed a model that uses a unique fusion of text and image features to predict categories by training a neural network to encode point-of-attractation data using pre-trained text and image encoders. By fine-tuning these encoders, we achieve state-of-the-art results on this new task.

The purpose of our research is to examine how listeners' reactions to the same financial news affect stock price stability through analyzing speech patterns and sentiment in transcribed company conference calls. This study compares a benchmark stock to its related assets over a 9-year period, tracking how corporate earnings influence stock value. To achieve this goal, we initially created a new dataset of transcribed company earnings calls spanning from 2012 to 2020, then utilized word embeddings and Deep Neural Networks to categorize speakers by sentiment and predict short-term stock fluctuations. This work is a starting point for exploring the connection between financial news impact and short-term stock price stability.

In the design of wireless sensor networks, effective sensor placement is critical for accurate monitoring and efficient coverage of a given area. This study investigates the optimal placement of sensors within a 2D environment, subject to communication range limitations. Two key factors were taken into account: the number of sensors required and individual sensor positions. Building upon existing research, this paper extends the solution to accommodate diverse sensor types with varying transmission ranges. A novel method for sensor placement is proposed, encompassing both homogeneous and heterogeneous sensor networks. For homogeneous networks, a mathematical model was developed to minimize the expected number of covered points, with a constraint on the number of sensors. A multi-step solution algorithm was designed to iteratively refine sensor positions, with a guarantee of convergence to a local optimum. For heterogeneous networks, a model was created to minimize the total covered area, with a constraint on the number of sensors. This model was solved using a combination of mathematical programming and simulated annealing. Results from both theoretical analysis and simulations confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed sensor placement strategies.

A new approach for filtering quantum eigenvalues based on polynomials with a lower complexity requirement than previous methods is introduced. This proposal offers an alternative to post-selection based algorithms like QDA and QEA, which filter out unwanted eigenvalues, while new "pre-selection" methods are presented for integrating the new filtering approach with existing algorithms. A quantum linear equations algorithm utilizing the new filtering approach and pre-selection method outperforms existing algorithms in most scenarios by eliminating the need for an additional classical step.

In the realm of self-dual theories, we examine compact $N=2$ $O(3) \times O(3)$ gauge field infant skyrmions, where the gauge group is enhanced by a non-linear 't Hooft-Polyakov type confinement mechanism. This leads to the establishment of a minimum size threshold for the skyrmions, a characteristic also found in other self-dual $N=2$ gauge fields, such as $\mathbb{CP}$ and $USp(2)$ cases. The compact gauged infant skyrmions exhibit unique properties, including a non-constant mean field, a non-integrable density function, and a non-constant energy density, in contrast to their unconfined counterparts. Moreover, we confirm that the compact gauged infant skyrmions possess a quantized size, in line with the Witten's $2\pi\mathbb{R}$-monopole charge.

This research delves into a new class of effective operators representing novel interactions, known as "novel four-body operators". They are significant in the Standard Model because they facilitate the detection of new physics beyond the Standard Model and are crucial for the electroweak baryogenesis theory. The study involves calculating the impact of these operators on various Standard Model processes, including the Higgs potential and several decay and production channels of Standard Model particles. The study uses the Standard Model Effective Field Theory to develop and interpret the results. The results are used to determine the constraints on the Wilson coefficients of the operators based on the data from multiple Standard Model particle colliders, including the LHC, Tevatron, and future colliders like the FCC-ee and HL-LHC, and makes predictions for the results. The study also investigates how future colliders can improve the constraints on the Wilson coefficients and uses the results to forecast the results. The study also makes predictions for the constraints on the Wilson coefficients for the other type of novel interactions, known as "novel five-body operators".

A rotating diamond sample with its nuclear moments aligned, created through optical polarization and subsequent nuclear spin orientation via the technique of optical nuclear hyperpolarization (ONH), has been demonstrated publicly for the first time. The diamond sample, which contains the isotope of $^{13}$C that is susceptible to this effect, allows for the long-term storage of its nuclear orientation. The diamond sample is encased within a sealed glass tube and has been showcased at the Paris International Research and Technology Fair 2015, appearing in several science publications. The exhibition highlights the potential of using $^{13}$C in solid state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) devices, including applications in quantum information processing.

Developing a whole-cell simulation that accurately models a cell's whole architecture hinges on a comprehensive and iterative process, requiring the integration of various components such as organelles, cells structures, and physical forces, in addition to biochemical reactions. A simulation framework like CellMorphDynamics has been developed to achieve this by applying the Multi-Compartment Reaction-Diffusion System to model cellular behavior. This framework utilizes a spatially explicit approach to simulate reactions and diffusion within cell compartments, allowing for a unified representation of organelles, cells structures, and physical forces. By employing a hybrid algorithm that combines multiple solvers, CellMorphDynamics enables the simulation of complex reactions and diffusion within cells, as well as interactions with the extracellular environment. A new benchmarking framework has been proposed to assess the accuracy of whole-cell simulations and facilitate the development of future frameworks.

Pictorious is a user-friendly, multi-view image search system that enables users to submit a query consisting of multiple images, and it automatically retrieves a collection of matching reference images along with relevant candidate images. The system is designed to be flexible and adaptable, allowing users to access it on various devices with different specifications, such as smartphones, tablets, or laptops, without compromising performance. To achieve this portability, the system utilizes a lightweight model that relies on a reduced version of the ResNet architecture, significantly minimizing memory allocation and computational demands. Additionally, the system incorporates a novel feature matching strategy that leverages the similarity between query and reference images to rank candidate image matches, and it computes these features using both GPU and CPU to expedite the search process. The system's effectiveness is demonstrated through a comprehensive evaluation on three multi-view image search datasets, showcasing its impressive retrieval performance.

Epilepsy affects one in twenty individuals worldwide, and the development of more reliable seizure prediction will greatly benefit people affected.  Using electroencephalogram (EEG) data, machine learning (ML) based approaches have been proven effective in detecting seizures, yet their performance often falters in real-world applications due to shifting baselines, variations in seizure patterns, and data contamination.  Hyperdimensional (HD) computing, a cutting-edge neuromorphic system, has shown potential in creating robust and efficient models that can learn and perform well on low-dimensional data.  In this study, we have applied HD techniques to enhance seizure detection in three key areas:  learning robust models, mitigating the effects of data contamination, and identifying seizure patterns that shift throughout the day.  Our results demonstrate that HD approaches outperform traditional ML methods, and the use of HD-based memory models significantly improve seizure prediction accuracy.  Our findings indicate that HD approaches can be leveraged to create more reliable seizure detection systems.

The LIGO-Virgo Collaboration has identified 93 gravitational wave (GW) events in the Deci-hertz region, with 79 of these detected within its sensitive frequency band. This research utilizes 79 GW events to estimate the Hubble constant ($H_0$) based on the 'inflationary gravitational standard model' (IGSM). Our findings indicate that the Hubble constant is significantly lower than that derived from the Planck data, specifically, we calculate $H_0 = 67.00 \pm 1.62$ Mpc-1. This is in line with recent measurements from the IGSR collaboration, which reported $H_0 = 67.54 \pm 1.74$ Mpc-1, and the SH0ES value of $H_0 = 73.24 \pm 1.75$ Mpc-1 based on the SNLS3 data. Furthermore, our research has successfully linked the IGSM Hubble constant to the inflationary energy scale (which is the energy scale of the universe at the time of inflation). We have also made a forecast for the GW events to be detected by the NANOGrav collaboration, which will enable further refinement of the IGSM Hubble constant. This research highlights the potential of GW events to be used as a valuable cosmological probe.

We have developed an enhanced version of QALD-9, a question-answering dataset composed of questions in English along with corresponding answers sourced from DBpedia. The updated version, QALD-9-plus, incorporates a diverse set of 1,069 English-to-English and 436 English-to-other language question-answer pairs, generated by native speakers, and includes accompanying answers derived from Wikidata. The QALD-9-plus dataset offers a rich multilingual resource for the Question Answering task of the DBpedia Challenge, initially established in 2015, and has been designed to facilitate comprehensive evaluation of QA systems across various languages. In this study, we outline the criteria for selecting target languages, presenting each question in multiple languages, and describe the methods employed for generating the QA pairs, as well as providing an in-depth analysis of the QA pairs generated. The QALD-9-plus dataset is publicly available at [QALD-9-plus website].

Human perception is inherently imperfect, susceptible to distractions and inconsistencies.
This leads to discrepancies in how we experience and interpret the world around us.
Our proposed framework aims to mitigate these discrepancies by using a memory-based approach
to compare and contrast recent experiences and generate a unified representation.
Key to this approach is a new algorithm that can learn from past experiences and adapt to new situations.
Experimental results on simulated data as well as real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness
of our framework in resolving perception discrepancies and offering a more accurate view.

To effectively use deep learning models in medical image analysis, it is crucial to first detect and address any implicit biases present in our models or data. Our research introduces a new method for detecting innate biases in medical image data by investigating how different demographic groups, including age and skin color, influence the outcomes of deep neural networks. We developed a straightforward test to verify the presence of innate biases in medical image datasets using a benchmark task and discovered that various public datasets contain biases despite not having labeled data. Our results demonstrate that the presence of innate biases can lead to inaccurate diagnoses. Furthermore, we found that the likelihood and implications of these biases vary depending on the type of model used, the specific medical task being performed, and the population being served.

This paper addresses the issue of noisy data within metric learning by developing a novel loss function. Metric learning loss functions are typically designed to concentrate similar and dissimilar instances together, with many recent advancements incorporating complex components like distance calculations and loss weights. However, existing loss functions often fail to effectively handle noisy data due to the influence of some data points. To resolve this problem, our proposed method, called Gentle Proxy-Anchor Loss, integrates a distillation loss to accurately determine the similarity between proxies and corresponding instances. Additionally, this loss incorporates a dynamic loss weight that adjusts its value based on the confidence level of each instance. Experiments on various datasets demonstrate that our proposed loss outperforms existing loss functions in metric learning applications.

The Gaussian random field theory has been utilized to derive the dependence of the 2-point correlation amplitude on the density field's spatial gradient weight in both flat and open Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker cosmological backgrounds. This relation, known as the 2PCF, offers a novel method for comparing theoretical models to observations of dark matter without making assumptions about how dark and luminous matter are correlated. By incorporating the power spectrum, the 2PCF can be expressed analytically. Key findings include the power-law dependence of the 2PCF on the gradient weight, which has been observed in N-body simulations and is consistent with the power spectrum. By applying the relation to observations of galaxies and galaxy clusters, it is possible to constrain the power spectrum, thereby bypassing the need for an estimate of galaxy bias. This approach also demonstrates the suitability of the relation for analyzing observations of large-scale structures, including the cosmic microwave background radiation.

We develop an underlying integrable framework for a two-dimensional, topological SO(5) superfluid model and provide analytical solutions for finite-range interactions between nearby spinor atoms. Furthermore, we investigate the behavior of a solution under specific long-range limits, which may be relevant to recent experiments involving polar molecules.

Micro-Phoswich Arrays with Dichroic Coatings and Photodiodes (MAPD) is a novel type of photodetector that combines a scintillator layer with an optical readout system. MAPD's design utilizes a photodetector that spans the scintillator's entire width, effectively doubling its detection area and doubling the potential for measuring scintillator properties. This results in a photodetector that captures the entire scintillation light flux, allowing for a precise measurement of the light flux's temporal characteristics. This particular application of MAPD makes it an ideal solution for the study of scintillation properties, particularly in the study of snowstorm detectors used in high-energy physics experiments, where scintillation light flux is measured to determine the characteristics of snowstorm detectors used in the study of neutrinos.

Given a Cohen-Macaulay local ring $(R, \mathfrak{m})$, we explore how the localized Hilbert series of $R$ relate to its minimal free resolutions and an associated homology matrix, specifically examining how changes in $R$ affect these properties. Specifically, we show that if $R$ is an equivariant complete intersection, the change in its Hilbert series upon localizing at a prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}$ is determined by the degrees of a set of specific polynomials, known as the Milnor numbers of $\mathfrak{p}$. We also prove that the Hilbert series of $R$ after localization can be expressed as a rational function with roots that are linked to the Frobenius exponents of $\mathfrak{m}$. These findings are further applied to the case where $R$ is an isolated singularity, yielding a formula that relates its Hilbert series after localization to the dimensions of specific graded pieces of its minimal free resolution.

A recent study using nuclear forward scattering examined the magnetic properties of Aurivillius Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ at elevated pressures. This oxide exhibits a complex structural arrangement, comprising alternating Aurivillius blocks and perovskite layers. X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that under high pressure, the material undergoes a phase transition from an orthorhombic phase to a tetragonal one at 0.65 (3)$\pm$ 0.02 (3) GPa, accompanied by a reduction in volume of approximately 1.5%. Neutron diffraction data showed that magnetic ordering occurs in the material under high pressure, with the magnetic structure being described as a $c$-axis ferromagnetic arrangement. This new magnetic phase was found to be highly stable, persisting even after being returned to ambient conditions. Notably, the material's magnetic ordering was found to be unaffected by high-pressure transformations, whereas the volume of the magnetic unit cell underwent significant changes. This suggests that the magnetic properties of the material are highly sensitive to the material's high-pressure transformations.

A comparative analysis of two Bayesian-type trading programs is conducted. The programs, known as BCP and BOP, operate within a framework characterized by constant trading fees every time a buy or sell action is taken, and their performance is evaluated in this context. The unique aspect of these programs is that they require periodic trading to avoid incurring significant penalties for prolonged holding without transactions. The BOP method is based on a Poisson distribution, whereas the BCP method is based on a normal distribution. Both methods are employed simultaneously with a single share of Apple stock as a benchmark to compare their historical performance. The BOP method is found to be more effective in this scenario. Furthermore, a ranking system is developed to evaluate the effectiveness of these programs under various trading conditions. The BOP method is found to be more effective in a wide range of cases, such as when a single share is involved, and certain conditions are met.

Optomechanical systems have been instrumental in developing highly efficient optomechanical devices such as optomechanical filters. In this study, we have created a fully adjustable optomechanical filter system that can be easily integrated with conventional optical circuitry. By utilizing a unique optomechanical filter design based on a directly connected optical resonator system, we have successfully developed a device that can be easily scaled up to achieve high transmission rates. As a proof of concept, we have developed a device that can be easily integrated with a fiber optic system to achieve high transmission rates of up to 90% with a low power optical signal of up to 0.12 micro watts.

Public health interventions are being implemented to curb the spread of infectious diseases like influenza, partly through education campaigns aimed at enhancing risk awareness. These efforts are subsequently promoted through media, with social media serving as a primary medium for public awareness and the press handling it for the general public. Analyzing social media and news articles can provide valuable insights into the impact of these educational interventions. This study proposes a two-pronged approach for evaluating the effectiveness of public health educational campaigns by assessing the impact on users' posts on social media and news articles coverage. A proposed method for calculating changes in users' posts and articles content related to relevant topics is also presented, utilizing a deep neural network classifier to identify whether a post or article contains a mention of the targeted topic. The study further discusses challenges and limitations associated with this approach, such as the availability of social media data, the reliability of content on social media and news articles, the need for relevant training data, and the potential for biased results.

The compression of image data is a pressing issue due to the exponential growth in image files, driven by advancements in technology that enable the creation of increasingly high-resolution images. While neural network-based compression methods have gained popularity, they often rely on complex, sequential processing that doesn't fully utilize modern computing hardware. To address this limitation, we've developed a neural network called PILC that provides an efficient, end-to-end solution for image compression, leveraging the capabilities of GPUs to achieve faster processing. By utilizing a novel, multi-scale network architecture that combines spatial and spectral information, PILC can accurately predict image blocks and encode them in compressed form. Experimental results demonstrate PILC's effectiveness, with performance metrics indicating superior compression capabilities compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

Using proton-proton collision data collected at various energy levels, specifically 7, 8, and 13 TeV at luminosities up to 50 fb$^{-1}$, the LHCb experiment detected and measured the branching fraction of the $B^{+}$ to $D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}$ decay. They also conducted an initial search for the $B^{+}$ to $D_s^{+}\phi$ decay. Measured branching fractions, specifically for the $B^{+}$ to $D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}$ and $B^{+}$ to $D_s^{+}\phi$ modes, were determined to be 7.7 to 4.4 to 4.6 (statistical) to 2.9 to 2.8 to 2.8 (statistical and systematic) times 10$^{-4}$. Furthermore, the $B^{+}$ to $D_s^{+}\phi$ decay was found to occur at a rate 0.81 times 0.71 (statistical) to 0.70 (statistical and systematic) times 10$^{-3}$, which represents a five standard deviation signal.

In the context of optimal transfer in quantum control, we examine the effects of an anomalous pulse that deviates from the ideal, well-tuned sequence, and derive an enhanced algorithm for mitigating this deviation by incorporating a corrective pulse. This improved method is more effective than conventional methods such as robust and robust-invariant techniques. The added value of the proposed approach is demonstrated through a comparison of the fidelity gains achieved in two well-known applications: precise entanglement generation and precise quantum state transfer.

This paper proposes a novel approach to developing artificial intelligence companions that work in harmony with humans by predicting their behavior using machine learning models, and then using reinforcement learning to refine these predictions. The authors developed a human decision-making model and utilized it to simulate various scenarios, and then trained a neural network to mimic the human partner's actions. The results demonstrate that the neural network learned behaviors comparable to humans, and in some cases, made more efficient decisions. The research also highlights potential areas for improvement, such as incorporating the human's perception into the model and employing more advanced learning methods. The findings suggest that the chosen approach is a viable starting point for creating adaptable AI partners that learn and evolve through interaction.

Researchers examine the intricacies of a comprehensive supersymmetric model that integrates a $B-L$ symmetry. This model's Higgs sector includes five doublets, while scalar singlets play a crucial role in stabilizing the model's vacuum. They delve into the lightest scalar neutralino's mass, an ongoing focus of both the LHC and future collider studies. This approach also encompasses the dark matter candidates, addressing both the composition of the WIMP and the generation of the baryon asymmetry within the universe. Researchers explore the model's phenomenology, highlighting its interrelated connections to electroweak baryogenesis and the model's gauge and flavour symmetry breaking patterns. A detailed discussion of the model's fine-tuning is provided, complemented by an extensive analysis of a simplified version that integrates a single heavy scalar neutralino.

This study examines task-related variations in spatial skills and performance with visualizations across different professions. Building on previous research which pinpointed a universal decline in performance with complex visualizations, this research investigates how various disciplines and fields may exhibit unique task-related differences in addition to universal patterns. A total of 1,740 participants from 25 distinct professions were tested on 4 tasks requiring spatial skills and visualizations, including the interpretation of 3D plots, bar charts, and large data sets. Results indicate that both profession and task have significant impacts on task performance, with specific professions like engineering and economics showing superior performance and those like marketing showing less skill. These findings suggest that professionals' skills and performance vary by task and profession, and highlight the need for tailored approaches to visualization design and education.

The increased interest in input selection methods for theorem provers has led to a range of techniques being developed, particularly for first-order logic. These methods aim to improve a theorem prover's performance by presenting it with more effective sets of premises. This study focuses on a specific type of input selection strategy known as clause collection, which is particularly useful in induction schemes with multiple base cases. These strategies are often used in the formal verification of embedded systems. A new technique from the field, called cycle detection, has been identified as a potential approach for enhancing clause collection strategies, and we have explored its application in this context. We have also conducted a series of experiments using the \systemc{} design system, which have shown that a cycle detection-based method can lead to improvements in the efficiency of hyper-resolution strategies in practical scenarios.

In information retrieval, a key task is graph matching. Given two graphs, one known and one unknown, along with a list of possible mappings, the goal is to determine which mapping is most accurate. Historically, this process has been approached as a ranking task where a model is asked to predict the accuracy of each mapping, but recent research suggests that this approach is flawed because it doesn't require the model to consider the entire graph, instead focusing on individual node comparisons. A new task is proposed where a model is trained to correct each mapping, resulting in significantly improved performance over traditional ranking-based tasks across four benchmark datasets.

Deep learning models often excel in predicting long-term patterns but struggle with short-term predictions, leading to concerns of their practicality. Pre-training techniques help mitigate this issue but may not entirely solve it. This study investigates the dynamics of linear stochastic systems and finds that training deep neural networks on these systems' long-term behaviors can effectively predict long-term transitions as well as short-term ones, demonstrating that learned models are robust to different training objectives. Furthermore, we analyze the benefits and drawbacks of various training techniques and propose new methods for modeling stochastic systems, which we test on a set of linear stochastic systems and their respective variants.

This research focuses on a specific type of generation dispatch models that incorporate a new form of electricity allocation using generation-specific constraints. These constraints are based on a sharing framework where each generator's output is divided fairly according to a well-defined formula. Our study examines the computational aspects of these constraints and reveals a limitation in the existing approach, leading to the development of more practical and efficient solutions to the dispatch problem. Notably, our proposed models exhibit greater robustness to changes in input data and are capable of handling large-scale optimization problems.

This study introduces a novel approach for identifying event instances that are related to the same underlying event. The focus is on non-cooccurring events connected by common themes, such as opposing views on a particular issue or event-related consequences. To address this challenge, we developed a two-stage framework that utilizes a transformer-based model to generate event representation vectors, which are then used by a self-attention mechanism to establish relationships between them. The approach was evaluated using a custom-dataset consisting of events related to the US Democratic Party's internal strife, demonstrating the model's ability to accurately resolve event coreference with an F1-score of 58%.

The Complementarity Knapsack Problem, a mixed-integer nonlinear program with complementarity constraints, is a challenging nonlinear program. Solving this issue can lead to intricate nonlinear and complementarity constraints that are difficult to optimize. To tackle this complexity, we've developed a new problem classification that utilizes special basis elements from complementarity constraints to break down the original problem. This multi-faceted approach is crucial for understanding and creating algorithms to solve the Complementarity Knapsack Problem effectively.

This paper defines and explores $I$-admissible derivations for $2\times2$ matrix algebras over Euclidean rings, introducing the concept of $I$-Jordan derivations that build upon ordinary derivations. $I$-Jordan derivations are linked to two types of centralizers - those for $I$-Jordan derivations and those for ordinary derivations - both of which are found to be right and left multiplicative. For semiprimery algebras, it is established that the centralizers for $I$-Jordan derivations and those for ordinary derivations are equivalent. Using this result, it is demonstrated that the set of $I$-admissible derivations within a semiprime algebra $R$ forms a nilpotent class with a nilpotency class size of at most $5$.

We derive Weinberg's 2-factor scattering amplitude for massless bosons within the framework of General Relativity, emerging naturally from the application of Stueckelberg field decoupling to the graviton field equations under specific spin constraints. The constraints are enforced via local Lorentz invariants, which also yield a gauge-invariant action principle. By decoupling, we obtain the Stueckelberg field's associated 2-particle operator, which corresponds to the graviton's dual tensor field. The terms within the action principle primarily consist of products of single-particle operators, which facilitate a systematic expansion of the dual tensor operator. The resulting scattering amplitude is found to be gauge-invariant up to order $\kappa^2$.

We define the transversal space $T_{\psi}$ as the set of all non-zero vectors in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ that remain at a minimum angle $\psi$ to a fixed subspace $V$. We examine the transversal group of a nonlinear projection onto $W$ within $T_{\psi}$. We focus on the case where $\psi = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $W$ is a $k$-dimensional subspace. We prove that the transversal group satisfies a specific property for any given non-zero vector $v \in T_{\pi / 2}$. We also show that the set of all vectors satisfying this property forms a group under the operation of scalar multiplication. We define the Favard length as the smallest positive real number $\psi$ such that the transversal space of a given subspace is a subset of $T_{\psi}$. We study the Favard length of projections onto subspaces of various dimensions and subspace dimensions. We provide numerical results for the smallest possible Favard length of projections onto two-dimensional subspaces.

We introduce a new approach to directed policy search, known as I-RTPS, that learns control policies for a variety of high-dimensional systems by efficiently navigating an extended version of an optimal tube region around an existing reference policy. By focusing on an adaptive tube region that grows as the policies are updated, I-RTPS overcomes the limitations of previous directed policy search methods which required a precise model of the system to optimize control policies. Our approach involves an online imitation learning stage where the algorithms learn from an initial, possibly suboptimal policy and adapt to optimize control performance without needing a precise model of the system. Furthermore, I-RTPS can efficiently update its parameters across a range of complex systems including high-dimensional mechanical and fluid systems. To showcase its effectiveness, we demonstrate I-RTPS on a range of complex systems, including a 3D quadcopter and a 4DOF vehicle, and it outperforms traditional directed policy search methods by a substantial margin, achieving a 10-30% improvement in tracking accuracy.

The unusual Hall effect, which arises at the first order due to spin-orbit coupling, is an unusual phenomenon. This is because it does not contain any power terms related to the spin-orbit coupling. Recent experiments have successfully observed the intrinsic unusual Hall effect in semiconductors at the third order, showing that it is not dependent on the spin-orbit coupling. This unusual phenomenon occurs independently of the spin-orbit coupling order and can be attributed to the third-order electron-phonon or electron-electron interaction. This work utilizes a semiclassical theory to predict the intrinsic unusual Hall effect at the third order, which is verified by the results of the work cited as reference \cite{Xiao:2019}.

The increasing use of software repositories has led to a surge in the development of techniques for analyzing software evolution. One such approach involves using call graph representations to compare the evolution of software families across various platforms. Nevertheless, these call graphs can be quite extensive, and analyzing them to compare software families is a computationally demanding task. In this study, we introduce a method for creating a compact representation of call graph sets that can be easily updated as new software revisions become available. We also propose a similarity metric for comparing these representations, which can be used to compare the evolution of software families across various platforms. The primary goal of this approach is to enable practitioners to quickly identify the most relevant aspects of the evolution of software families, thereby facilitating their development and maintenance.

The Donahues et al. text classification benchmark, featuring one billion words of text across five categories, has been credited with driving significant progress in text classification models. While this is true, researchers have expressed concerns about the benchmark's training protocol and the types of models it encourages. In this study, we challenge the benchmark's validity by demonstrating that it promotes a narrow, uninformative approach to learning categorization. This is achieved by modeling the distribution of a single label while maintaining independent distributions for the remaining labels, resulting in the lowest possible Bayes risk across all labels. Our findings also show that the same strategy is effective when applied to the more commonly used Amazon Reviews benchmark, highlighting a potential flaw in the current evaluation methods.

High-resolution X-ray flares are caused by magnetic reconnection within turbulent current sheets, resulting in various non-standstill plasma patterns such as plasmoids and vortices.  The standard flare model, however, fails to account for the quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) observed in flare emissions, which could be linked to periodic movements of these plasma patterns.  To investigate this connection, a new simulation involving a complex current sheet in a vacuum has been performed.  The results show the formation of dynamic plasma structures and their associated QPOs in radio and X-ray emissions, which can be attributed to flapping and rolling motions of these structures.  The QPOs in different frequency bands display unique characteristics, with their periods and amplitudes varying significantly.  The simulation also reveals that the QPOs can be linked to varying levels of Alfvénic turbulence in different plasma regions, which can be used to infer the underlying plasma conditions.

This paper outlines a multi-scale anomaly identification method suitable for evaluating the quality of industrial components with irregular shapes, focusing on extracting key geometric characteristics such as volume, boundary surface area, and convex surface area. The method employs an active contour approach driven by an energy function that integrates differences between an initial model and the target object. Due to the complex nature of such objects, a first-order optimization strategy is often insufficient, prompting the use of a higher-order Total Variation regularizer to mitigate the lack of smoothness in the contour. The proposed approach is demonstrated using a diverse set of test objects, including complex shapes such as cast iron blooms, for which geometric characteristics are crucial in downstream industrial applications, such as shell casting.

The study focuses on a modified KP-I equation incorporating a small, complex parameter that accounts for irregular initial conditions with a specific degree of complexity. Within a specific range of the parameter, this study shows that the equation's solutions become stable and remain consistent over time. Additionally, this study quantifies the degree of complexity in the initial conditions that are compatible with the equation's dynamics. Furthermore, this study quantifies the degree of complexity in the solutions and generalizes a result from a previous study to include the effects of dispersion.

The loss of degeneracy in Kramers' theorem, which occurs in stable non-secular complex multilevel systems with time-reversal symmetry, is investigated in systems that are not completely closed and can interact with their surroundings. This investigation reveals that, even in the absence of complete isolation, the degeneracy can still be broken in the system's equilibrium state when it has a non-zero temperature. The degeneracy can be broken in the system's steady-state due to thermal energy exchange between the system and its environment. However, the degeneracy remains intact in the system's pure quantum states, regardless of how strongly the system interacts with its surroundings. The research also demonstrates that, by isolating the system from thermal energy exchange, the degeneracy can be restored. This restoration occurs when the system undergoes a transformation that brings it back to its original, non-degenerate state. The research provides a clear understanding of the interplay between the system's interactions and its degeneracy, which can be applied to various real-world systems, including magnetic systems and quantum dots.

In highly mobile environments, accurately predicting future channel state information (CSI) responses is crucial for enhancing the efficiency of uplink transmissions in such scenarios. A novel approach to parameterize and forecast CSI dynamics for mobile users is proposed, leveraging an auto-regressive dynamic model (ARDM) that incorporates spatial and temporal dependencies. This model enables the representation of CSI responses as a function of spatial, temporal, and spatial-temporal factors. Subsequently, ARDM's parameters are estimated using an online version of the Kalman filter, and forecasting is performed using past CSI responses and spatial-temporal factors. A comparison with existing state-of-the-art forecasting methods demonstrates the efficacy of our proposed method.

We present a novel approach for determining the size of a region of interest within an image, represented by a single color value. This size estimation is facilitated through the use of a mixture model consisting of Beta components with varying parameters. Two key advantages of this B-mixture model arise. Firstly, it allows us to estimate key parameters, including the mixture count and component weights, as well as the relevant area, through a mathematical optimization process within a 2D space. Secondly, this model enables us to make inferences about the distribution of color values, including their mean and standard deviation, at a given location within the image. We propose a method for estimating these parameters using a hierarchical Bayesian framework, where the posterior distribution of the model parameters given the image data is represented by a Dirichlet-Generalized Beta distribution. We demonstrate that this posterior distribution can be sampled efficiently using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo method, based on Gibbs sampling and slice sampling. We have successfully tested our approach using stereo vision ground truth data, and our experimental findings are presented below.

This study expands upon earlier work by Ma and Pokorný, examining how the Szegő energy of a Grauert tube over a CR structure evolves as the radius increases without bound. The research demonstrates that this energy measure has a predictable limit under two conditions: when the volume of the base CR structure is finite, and when the dimension of the Grauert tube corresponds to its dimension as a complex manifold. In this latter case, the limiting energy measure is equivalent to the total scalar curvature of the asymptotically hyperbolic space, a finding that has practical implications for calculating the volume of Grauert tubes in relation to the scalar curvature of the original, bounded CR structure.

In 1979, G. Guirardello introduced the concept of reverse line chart (RLC), which is an effective way to visualize data, especially for long-term trends. A novel approach to creating RLCs, called the matrix redesigning algorithm (MARINLINGA), has been developed, along with a comparison to the widely used method by S. Roussopoulos from 1971. A mathematical simulation using RLCs with artificial data demonstrates that MARINLINGA produces a more accurate representation than Roussopoulos's technique when the data set is sufficiently large.
Building on Lee-Lee's hypothesis that the category of rigid modules over a commutative ring has a finite topological dimension, we present a proof strategy and confirm the hypothesis holds true.

Accurately estimating memory usage for Java programs is a complex task, particularly considering the impact of transient data on heap allocation. Recent research has shown that soft, hard, and strong references have distinct properties. However, the focus has been limited to short-term analysis. Our study extends this perspective by investigating the evolution of these reference types over an extended period. Our research is based on 1,189 popular open-source repositories, which exhibit diverse characteristics such as varying codebase sizes, reference types, and compilation strategies. By analyzing these repositories, we found that the number of transient data objects grows at a slower rate than code evolution, with transient data accounting for up to 20% and 40% of total references, respectively. Furthermore, our results indicate that compilation methods have a limited effect on the reference types. Our study also reveals that the proportion of transient data evolves at a predictable rate across various stages of code development. This discovery enables developers to adjust their memory allocation strategies according to the stage of code growth.

In a study on entangling two-qubit systems using quantum interference and wave mixing techniques, researchers identified two distinct pathways. One pathway involves entanglement buildup through wave mixing, while the other achieves entanglement instantly, despite significant quantum fluctuations. The instant entanglement pathway relies on entangling two qubits in a single quantum event, followed by de-excitation. The wave mixing pathway exhibits non-Markovian behavior, allowing the two qubits to recombine and strengthen their entanglement, thereby reducing the influence of quantum fluctuations. The two pathways have opposing effects on entanglement: the wave mixing pathway enhances it, whereas the pathway involving a single quantum event degrades it. The relative influence of these pathways depends on the entangled biphotons' overlap, with the wave mixing pathway dominating at high overlap but the single quantum event pathway taking over at low overlap. The single quantum event pathway can be leveraged to enhance entanglement, exploiting the rivalry between the two pathways.

This paper explores a type of stochastic optimization issue known as multistage distributionally resilient optimization. In this context, an operator makes sequential decisions to mitigate potential disruptions caused by an adversary. The authority's goal is to minimize costs across multiple stages, while the adversary aims to maximize them. Each stage's uncertainty is represented as a probability distribution, and the authority has access to a stream of data about these distributions, which can utilize to inform its decisions. A new method has been developed that involves selecting specific scenarios from the future distributional uncertainty set at each stage to serve as reference points for the authority's decision-making process. These reference points are chosen based on a measure of discrepancy that takes into account the authority's risk tolerance and the likelihood of the adversary's distribution. The method has been proven to be robust and has been tested in a numerical setting involving a supply chain network that is sensitive to disruptions.

Recently, researchers have been working to predict actions in order to anticipate the future evolution of semi-autonomous vehicles and robots, thereby enhancing their decision-making capabilities. To address this issue, we propose an innovative neural network architecture that uses a feature mapping approach with Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernels to effectively model sequential data. Our proposed model, called k-RNN, incorporates a kernel layer that maps initial sequences to a new, feature-rich space using RBF kernels and then employs a recurrent neural network to generate future sequence representations. We test our model on action recognition and future prediction tasks and show that it outperforms existing methods, even when working with limited data.

We investigate the single-component, one-dimensional lattice Landau-Ginzburg model, an exactly solvable representation of a thermalization scenario. By coupling it with a higher-dimensional harmonic oscillator, we develop a two-dimensional potential landscape, where the ground state corresponds to a first-order transition within the thermalization framework. Analyzing the spectrum reveals three distinct regions, characterized by unique timescales that support the thermalization process. Furthermore, we introduce a lattice deformation as an adiabatic change of the external parameter, resulting in non-equilibrium dynamics. By analyzing the temporal evolution of the oscillator's momentum, we identify three distinct timescales associated with the prethermal, thermalization, and equilibration phases. Interestingly, the thermalization transition in this framework occurs between the prethermal and equilibration phases, occurring at a time scale that is polynomial rather than exponential, unlike traditional thermalization scenarios.

Consider a homogeneous tree of infinite depth and infinite breadth as the space X, and define the pseudo-differential operator $\sigma$ from the pre-Cauchy space of smooth functions on X to the Cauchy space of infinitely differentiable functions on X. We establish that the boundedness of $\sigma$ is equivalent to $\sigma$ being a Helton-Howe operator, and further demonstrate that the pseudo-differential operator $\sigma$ possesses nuclear properties if it is composed with a Laplacian-like operator on the tree.

The widespread adoption of mobile devices has significantly impacted network traffic. Recent studies have investigated the distinct characteristics of mobile devices by analyzing network traffic, yet a crucial aspect often goes unexplored - the visibility of devices through smartphone apps. This paper examines the extent to which different types of devices, including smartphones, laptops, and other devices, are visible in a mobile network. We collected and analyzed data from multiple users over three months in a mobile network, utilizing a cutting-edge, invisible monitoring approach. We found that smartphones dominate network activity, even in 5G mobile networks, and are visible in the network for a longer duration. Laptops pose a concern as their network activity is highly unpredictable and may remain undetected in the network for a long time.

Machine learning models tend to overconfidently generate images far from the training data set, leading to inaccurate performance guarantees in real-world scenarios. This issue is particularly problematic in various applications, including autonomous vehicles, medical imaging, and autonomous flight control systems. To address this challenge, we have developed a comprehensive benchmark called CODEs, which assesses image-based generative models' real-world performance. By introducing a diverse set of real and synthetic challenges, we have designed five sub-benchmarks that target specific aspects of out-of-distribution data, including low-contrast, high-contrast, occlusions, shape distortions, and mixed priors. Our analysis of four leading generative models across these sub-benchmarks reveals real-world performance degradation and high variability among challenges. Additionally, we have proposed a simple and effective post-processing technique to reduce overconfidence and improve model performance. Our research provides a foundation for advancing the development of reliable generative models.

The CDF collaboration conducted a groundbreaking study on the angular relationships between the axes of individual partons or jets in high-energy proton-proton collisions at 1.96 TeV, using data collected with a specific detector setup. Although they found that the angular distributions between the axes of four individual partons in these collisions matched the predictions of perturbative QCD for a specific energy cutoff, their findings for energy-cutoff predictions differed from those anticipated by next-to-leading logarithmic resummation methods. Conversely, their measurements of the angular distributions between the axes of four jets matched the predictions of a specific theoretical model but those for 2-jet and 3-jet axes did not. Instead, their findings for these jet axes differed from predictions by single-logarithmic resummation methods but matched the predictions of another, more advanced theoretical model known as the back-reaction model.

The application of deep machine learning in image classification and recognition has been a major focus in recent years. Notably, the development of semi-supervised learning (SSL) has been a prominent area of research, given the challenges associated with acquiring large datasets for machine learning models. In this paper, we will explore the history and advancements of deep learning and semi-supervised learning. Additionally, we will examine prominent SSL techniques and their associated methods, including the use of generative models. The study will also examine recent innovations in semi-supervised learning, including its application in computer vision tasks. Furthermore, we will discuss the related field of unsupervised learning (USL) and its potential connections to SSL.

Current outlier detection methods rely on a single threshold for assessing model performance in learning density distributions. However, we argue that using a single threshold is insufficient to accurately evaluate the density model. To address this issue, we introduce RECol, a framework that utilizes reconstruction error metrics to evaluate outlier detection. Empirical evidence shows that different metrics are influenced by outliers to varying degrees, depending on the data distribution and the learned density model. By combining multiple metrics, we can achieve more accurate representations of data points as in-distribution or out-of-distribution. Theoretical insights also support the use of multiple metrics in this context. The experiments demonstrate that RECol significantly improves the accuracy of anomaly detection models, leading to improved performance in real-world scenarios.

We examine a class of non-linear Young-type equations within the context of higher-order derivatives. The theory is built by adapting and expanding on existing findings from previous studies on linear equations, with the majority of the proofs mirroring or closely aligning with their linear counterparts. A few novel approaches are necessary to address the non-linear aspects, with the majority of the general results being uniform, meaning they apply across a broad range of exponents. These findings are leveraged to analyze a non-linear analogue of the $p$-Laplacian operator, leading to the derivation of uniform bounds for solutions to specific classes of degenerate elliptic equations, both in terms of the weak $L^\infty$ theory and its strengthened version.

The Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) is used to investigate the Standard Model's limitations and to derive predictions for low-energy physics. By employing a dimension-six effective Lagrangian, we investigate the effects of specific SMEFT operators on neutrino mass and mixing. Specifically, we analyze the impact of two-dimensional-six power variations on neutrino spin and polarization, taking into account the most recent experimental data on neutrino spin effects during spin precession. Two of the examined operators have significant implications for neutrino mass and mixing, while the third has minimal effects. Using the constraints provided by the Dirac nature of the neutrinos and the requirement for hermiticity, we derive the most up-to-date estimates for the power variations, which are found to be in the order of one to two times $10^{- -3}$ for the first two operators and less than $10^{- -18}$ for the third.

In a recent paper, the dynamic relationship between neurons and glial cells was explored to understand the role of the glial network in the brain. A model that links these cells to a Wilson-Coupled Oscillator was developed, enabling the creation of complex rhythms. This paper delves deeper, presenting a simplified version of the model that replicates the same dynamic. A mean-field approach to the Gliox model was introduced, allowing for the derivation of a coupled oscillator equation. Notably, this basic model exhibits a diverse array of patterns, ranging from simple unison to complex chaos and various types of rhythmic behavior. This simplified model provides new insights into the rhythmic behavior of the original neuron-glial system.

In a vacuum with a background magnetic field, a neutral spin-1/2 particle is studied for its unique properties. This system's Hamiltonian is derived from the Dirac equation, resulting in a pseudo-spin operator that defines its topological states. The topological states are characterized by a Berry phase, even for particles with a spin of 1/2. The presence of a background magnetic field introduces a magnetic flux through which the particle can access different energy levels. The system's behavior is calculated in the presence of this non-Abelian effect, yielding a non-Abelian geometric phase. The system's non-Abelian properties are explored in detail.

We are studying a one-dimensional, infinite lattice where particles interact in non-overlapping, $m$-copy neighborhoods. Each site can hold up to $m$ particles, and adjacent sites exchange particles based on a simple, locally linear rule. Particles leave one site and enter another at a rate determined by the difference in their values, with the rate being a function of the site's position and the number of particles there. Our goal is to determine the long-term, steady-state distribution of the number of particles on the boundary, and we found that this distribution depends heavily on the size of the neighborhood $m$.

Kawauchi initially proposed the concept of a formal semigroup to represent the crossing information in a link diagram. Building on Green's classification, we found a specific type of hyperbolic link that satisfies an important condition, allowing us to determine if its formal semigroup is "integral" by analyzing its link complement's fundamental group. We discovered that the "integral" formal semigroups correspond to hyperbolic L-space links, providing a critical constraint. Moreover, for a specific type of hyperbolic link, we found a direct relationship between its formal semigroup and the combinatorial properties of the link's diagram. This relationship allows us to identify and classify hyperbolic L-space links based on their formal semigroups, leading to the discovery of a new class of hyperbolic links, which we call "conjugate-reversible," and show that these links have a direct relationship with the properties of their surface boundary links.

We have developed a method to construct Poisson maps in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, specifically for the Lorentz gas, using its phase space and a space of orbits defined by forward and backward semi-flows. This approach enables the creation of Poisson maps with a non-constant spatial disorder for models of particles with memory or those in a non-stationary state. Employing the non-autonomous Boltzmann equation, we have derived a semigroup map from macroscopic diffusion equations to velocity-dependent diffusion equations from discrete models. This study also includes numerical examples of non-equilibrium ensembles of billiards with moving boundaries or changing spatial disorder, illustrating various nonequilibrium properties like current and off-diagonal elements in diffusion matrices. This work has implications for understanding nonequilibrium transport theories and their relation to nonequilibrium hydrodynamics.

Endoscopic techniques utilizing natural orifice transluminal imaging (NOIS) to examine the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) are associated with several risks, including perforation, bleeding, and infection. To minimize these complications, real-time monitoring of endoscopic tools and objects is crucial. By integrating real-time object detection in endoscopic video streams, this risk can be mitigated. Our study investigates the effectiveness of an object detection system by comparing multiple models and tools. We trained and evaluated four object detection models, including SqueezeDet, RetinaNet, SSD, and F-RCNN, on the Endoscopic Tool Artefact Dataset (ETAD). Our results indicate that the best-performing tool detection model achieved impressive accuracy, detection speed, and precision. Additionally, we developed a tool detection system that seamlessly integrates the tool boundary detection capability. Our tool detection system, optimized for real-time processing, achieved high performance, with 96.2% accuracy, 42.4 frames per second processing speed, and 90.1% detection precision.

In software engineering, understanding the components of a program is a vital aspect. This study delves into specific program elements like class names, method names, and variable names to uncover their underlying patterns and relationships. Through a substantial analysis of 10,000 highly-regarded open-source Java packages, the researchers uncover and dissect the prevalent syntax patterns found in element identifiers. Furthermore, a semantic layer is applied to these patterns to reveal their core meanings. This semantic layer is then utilized to identify patterns associated with software defects, with the results showing that these patterns indeed correlate with errors.

We create a new infinite-dimensional $\square_q$-structure derived from the affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, utilizing the $q$-Dixmier-Malliavin algebra and the affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ number system. This new structure is a generalization of the $\square_q$-structure developed from the $q$-Dixmier-Malliavin algebra by different authors. Our construction also relies on the introduction of a $q$-analog of the Maclaurin's series for generating functions.

The data analysis reveals that adding a third pure grain component to a binary (2-3) grain-growth system results in a minimal change in growth rate, thus validating the predicted kinematic relationship for a multi-component system with one coarsening mode. This outcome is unexpectedly straightforward, contrasting with the significant differences observed in shape evolution between binary and triplex systems. Consequently, the triplex system can be treated similarly to the binary system from the perspective of grain-growth kinetics.

Significant advancements in 3D human pose and shape recovery techniques have been achieved through the development of novel algorithms, but the field's progress has largely been evaluated based on datasets and their corresponding annotations. The crucial question of why certain datasets hold more significance than others and how their annotations impact the field's progress are often overlooked. To address these gaps, this paper introduces a holistic framework that considers not only datasets but also algorithms, sensors, and the underlying assumptions behind these techniques. A novel metric, the field's diversity, is proposed to measure innovation and progress in 3D human pose and shape recovery, encompassing diverse perspectives and perspectives. The study reveals that the top-ranked methods often rely on similar datasets and share similar assumptions, despite recent advancements in the field. The research also highlights the potential of 3D human pose and shape recovery to be applied in various fields, but most methods focus on a single domain, often relying on manual, dataset-specific annotations and neglecting domain generalization. The authors conclude that the field's progress would be significantly accelerated if more diverse and sensor-agnostic datasets were created and made available for research.

In the context of strong electron-electron interaction, a minimal two-dimensional lattice model is examined to assess superconductivity. This model posits the presence of sites and the hopping mechanism 'incoherent' and 'coherent' configurations, along with on-site and nearest-neighbor electron-electron interaction parameters $u$ and $u'$, respectively. It is assumed that $u$ is significantly less than $u'$. By analyzing this model, a critical analysis of the superconducting phase diagram is conducted, revealing stability regions with varying degrees of superconductivity. Notably, in the limit of strong $u'$ and $u$, two distinct superconducting phases emerge, characterized by non-Fermi-liquid behavior.

To develop accurate predictions for various colliders, it is essential to have a comprehensive and consistent set of parton distribution functions (PDFs) that incorporate the effects of new physics elements. A crucial component in this prediction process involves adjusting the PDFs to align with the new physics effects. This paper outlines a method for enhancing the OpenLoops PDFSet tool, enabling it to generate unified PDF sets that encompass both Standard Model and non-standard model physics operators simultaneously. This integration facilitates the incorporation of numerous scalar leptoquark models, allowing for a detailed exploration of theoretical parameters. As a proof of concept, the analysis includes a specific leptoquark model, dubbed A4-eta_1, which features global scalar leptoquark interactions.

This work presents an in-depth exploration of the connections between the theory of classification and modern machine learning, with the goal of developing innovative perspectives within this rapidly evolving field. Building upon the most cutting-edge methods in theory and practice, we delve into how various learning theory concepts apply to both contemporary and forthcoming forms of machine learning. Our discussion covers topics such as the trade-off between complexity and risk, the limits of sample representation, the distribution-free approach, the use of random features and random ensembles, and recent advancements in optimization techniques. Furthermore, we address the importance of generalization capabilities, identify potential areas for future research, and highlight the value of advanced mathematical concepts, such as spectral theory and functional analysis, in providing insightful solutions to the complex challenges faced in modern machine learning.

A widely applied control algorithm known as sliding mode control has a robust characteristic, but it often generates high levels of vibration and chattering in systems. This unwanted chattering can cause instability in systems that are sensitive, and it may prevent the system from achieving precise goals. This paper presents a new control strategy, terminal sliding mode control, which is specifically designed to enhance stability and precision in systems. By combining terminal attractor concept with sliding mode control, this approach aims to create a state space that is stable and free of oscillations, and to eliminate chattering effects by reaching zero-order crossing points in a short period of time.

The performance of lithium-ion batteries is significantly affected by the arrangement of their internal components, particularly within their active material systems. To accurately assess the impact of these internal structures on a battery's performance, we utilize a novel approach that involves applying ultrasonic vibrations to the electrodes and monitoring the resulting fluctuations in resistance. By analyzing the distinct patterns of these resistance oscillations, we are able to quantify the levels of segregation present within the electrodes on a micro-scale, accounting for the movement of lithium ions. Our findings show that the sensitivity of these oscillations is influenced by the size of the oscillations and the frequency at which they are applied. Moreover, we demonstrate that these oscillations can reveal the characteristics of the lithium-ion segregation within the anode on larger scales. Our results also suggest that these oscillations can be used to monitor changes in the electrodes over time, allowing us to establish a reliable timeline for the development of segregation within the anode as the battery ages.

This study focuses on designing and implementing a discrete-time tracking control system to precisely move a gantry crane under various conditions. Building on the concept of flatness-based control, the research identifies input profiles that allow a ganoy crane to follow a specific reference trajectory in both continuous and discrete-time formats.
